Ordinary relative paths. A literal "../" is a relative path, not an attack,
and before this was narrowed it failed 254 of 388 real HTML files and 27 of 88
real Makefiles -- quarantining a repository for containing documentation.

  CFLAGS += -I../include
  VPATH = ../src
  <a href="../commands/index.html">Commands</a>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="../_static/style.css">
  from ..models import User
  require('../package.json')
  #include "../common/defs.h"
  cd .. && make
  sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(__file__) + "/..")

Path arithmetic on a known directory variable is not traversal either. Joining
a build path with ".." to walk up one level is how every CMake project finds a
sibling directory; matching it failed 23 of 1116 real CMake files.

  set(DIR "${resolved_dir}/../lib")
  include("${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../common.cmake")
  list(APPEND CMAKE_MODULE_PATH "${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/../cmake")
  get_filename_component(ABS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../${FILE}" ABSOLUTE)
